detail.drainCleaning.intro1: Blocked drains are one of the most common household problems in Riyadh, especially with grease build-up in kitchen drains and soap or hair residue in bathroom drains. Ignoring a minor blockage lets it gradually worsen into overflow or a persistent bad smell, and the added pressure can eventually cause a leak at the drain connections.
detail.drainCleaning.intro2: At Homes Maintenance Solution we handle every level of blockage, from surface drains to the main sewer line connected to the public network, using high-pressure water-jetting equipment and internal inspection cameras when needed.
detail.drainCleaning.sign1: Slow water drainage in the sink or bathtub despite no visible blockage
detail.drainCleaning.sign2: Gurgling sounds from a drain or toilet whenever another drainage point is used
detail.drainCleaning.sign3: Recurring bad odor rising from drains despite regular cleaning
detail.drainCleaning.sign4: Repeated overflow at the same spot every few weeks despite manual clearing
detail.drainCleaning.step1desc: We identify the type and location of the blockage through a visual check and, when needed, a drain inspection camera.
detail.drainCleaning.step2desc: A mechanical drain snake for simple blockages, or high-pressure water jetting for stubborn clogs and built-up grease.
detail.drainCleaning.step3desc: We clear the blockage and clean the entire line, not just the clogged spot, to stop the problem coming back.
detail.drainCleaning.step4desc: We run water for several minutes to confirm normal drainage has fully returned before ending the visit.
detail.drainCleaning.faq1q: Does drain cleaning require breaking floors?
detail.drainCleaning.faq1a: In the vast majority of cases, no. We use mechanical drain snakes and water-jetting equipment that reach deep into the line without any need to break through surfaces, turning to structural solutions only in very rare cases such as damage to the pipe itself.
detail.drainCleaning.faq2q: How long does clearing a single drain take?
detail.drainCleaning.faq2a: Clearing one drain or floor trap usually takes 30 to 60 minutes, while clearing the main sewer line can take one to two hours depending on the line's length and the severity of the blockage.
detail.drainCleaning.faq3a: Yes, we recommend avoiding pouring oils and grease down the drain, installing hair strainers in floor drains, and scheduling preventive cleaning every 6-12 months for heavily used kitchens.
detail.leakDetection.intro1: A hidden water leak is one of the most damaging plumbing problems because it keeps harming the building for a long time without being noticed — from an unexplained spike in the water bill to damaged foundations, ruined paintwork, and mold.
detail.leakDetection.intro2: At Homes Maintenance Solution we rely on modern electronic and thermal leak-detection equipment that pinpoints the leak's location to within centimeters, without any need for random breaking into walls or floors.
detail.leakDetection.sign1: A sudden, unexplained spike in the monthly water bill
detail.leakDetection.sign2: Damp patches or discoloration on walls, ceilings, or floors
detail.leakDetection.sign3: A faint sound of running water even with every tap turned off
detail.leakDetection.sign4: A persistent damp or musty smell in one room with no obvious cause
detail.leakDetection.step1desc: We review the water bill and the home's meter to confirm whether a leak actually exists and estimate its size.
detail.leakDetection.step2desc: We use acoustic listening devices and thermal cameras to pinpoint the leak's location with high accuracy.
detail.leakDetection.step3desc: We mark the exact fault point before any intervention, to minimize or completely avoid breaking into surfaces.
detail.leakDetection.step4desc: We repair the leak point, then re-check the meter to confirm the leak has stopped completely.
detail.leakDetection.faq1q: How do I know I have a hidden water leak?
detail.leakDetection.faq1a: The easiest way is to close every tap and appliance in the house and watch the water meter for two hours; if it keeps moving, that's a strong sign of a leak.
detail.leakDetection.faq2q: Does the leak-detection equipment work with all pipe types?
detail.leakDetection.faq2a: Yes, our equipment works with PVC, PPR, and copper pipes alike, whether they're buried in walls, under floors, or in the ceiling.
detail.leakDetection.faq3q: Does detection also cover sewer line leaks?
detail.leakDetection.faq3a: Yes, we also offer sewer-line leak detection using specialized internal inspection cameras alongside drinking-water leak detection.
detail.pipeInstallation.intro1: Whether you're building a new home or renovating an old, corroded water network, the quality of the pipe installation is the foundation that determines the lifespan of the entire plumbing system.
detail.pipeInstallation.intro2: At Homes Maintenance Solution we use high-quality, standards-compliant PPR and PVC pipes, with tight welds and connections that prevent future leaks, whether for a complete new installation or repairing a damaged section of an existing network.
detail.pipeInstallation.sign1: Rust or discoloration in the water coming out of the tap
detail.pipeInstallation.sign2: Noticeably weak water pressure at one specific point and not others
detail.pipeInstallation.sign3: Knocking or vibration sounds inside the walls when taps are opened
detail.pipeInstallation.sign4: Repeated leaks at the same fitting despite a previous repair
detail.pipeInstallation.step1desc: We inspect the condition of the current pipes and decide which sections need full replacement versus a partial repair.
detail.pipeInstallation.step2desc: PPR for hot and cold water lines, or PVC for drainage lines, depending on the intended use.
detail.pipeInstallation.step3desc: We carry out welding and connections to safety standards, ensuring a fully tight seal with no weak points.
detail.pipeInstallation.step4desc: We test the line at a pressure higher than normal operation to confirm it's leak-free before handover.
detail.pipeInstallation.faq1q: What's the difference between PPR and PVC pipes?
detail.pipeInstallation.faq1a: PPR pipes are designed for pressurized hot and cold water lines and withstand high heat, while PVC pipes are mostly used for sewer and drainage lines where there's no pressurized hot water.
detail.pipeInstallation.faq2q: Can one section of the network be repaired without replacing the whole line?
detail.pipeInstallation.faq2a: Yes, in most cases the damaged section alone can be isolated and replaced without affecting the rest of the network, unless there's a general corrosion issue requiring a full re-pipe.
detail.pipeInstallation.faq3q: How long does installing a new water network for a whole home take?
detail.pipeInstallation.faq3a: It depends on the home's size and number of points, but it typically takes one to three working days for an average-sized apartment or house.
detail.waterHeaterService.intro1: The water heater is one of the most heavily used appliances in daily life, and any fault in it directly affects the comfort of the home.
detail.waterHeaterService.intro2: At Homes Maintenance Solution we offer a complete service covering installation of tank and tankless heaters, their routine maintenance, and repair of common faults such as weak heating, tank leaks, or thermostat and heating-element problems.
detail.waterHeaterService.sign1: Weak or fluctuating water temperature between hot and cold during use
detail.waterHeaterService.sign2: Water leaking from underneath or around the tank
detail.waterHeaterService.sign3: An unusual boiling or crackling sound coming from inside the heater
detail.waterHeaterService.sign4: A noticeably long wait for hot water to reach the tap
detail.waterHeaterService.step1desc: We check the heating element, thermostat, safety valve, and the condition of the tank's interior.
detail.waterHeaterService.step2desc: We remove calcium deposits inside the tank that reduce heating efficiency over time.
detail.waterHeaterService.step3title: Repairing or Replacing the Faulty Part
detail.waterHeaterService.step3desc: We replace the heating element, thermostat, or safety valve as needed, using original parts.
detail.waterHeaterService.step4desc: We run the heater and measure heating time and temperature to confirm it's back to safe, normal performance.
detail.waterHeaterService.faq1q: How often should a water heater be serviced?
detail.waterHeaterService.faq1a: We recommend preventive maintenance every 12 months to clear scale build-up and check the safety valve, especially in hard-water areas like Riyadh.
detail.waterHeaterService.faq2q: My heater is leaking from the bottom — does that mean it needs full replacement?
detail.waterHeaterService.faq2a: Not necessarily; in many cases the cause is a drain valve or a damaged fitting that can be easily replaced, and we determine that after a direct inspection before any decision to replace the whole tank.
detail.waterHeaterService.faq3q: What's the maintenance difference between tank and tankless heaters?
detail.waterHeaterService.faq3a: Tank heaters need periodic maintenance for calcium scale and heating-element checks, while tankless heaters mainly need flow-sensor and thermostat checks — we provide specialized maintenance for both types.
detail.waterPumpService.intro1: Weak water pressure on upper floors or frequent supply cuts are usually caused by a fault in the water pump or the pressure tank.
detail.waterPumpService.intro2: At Homes Maintenance Solution we install and maintain pressure pumps and ground-tank well pumps, with precise pressure settings tailored to the building's number of floors and actual consumption.
detail.waterPumpService.sign1: Weak water pressure on upper floors compared with the ground floor
detail.waterPumpService.sign2: The pump repeatedly switching on and off with no actual water use
detail.waterPumpService.sign3: Unusually loud vibration or noise while the pump is running
detail.waterPumpService.sign4: The pump stopping completely or not responding when a tap is opened
detail.waterPumpService.step1desc: We first identify the source of the problem: the pump itself, the air pressure tank, or the pressure switch.
detail.waterPumpService.step2desc: We inspect the motor, the electrical capacitor, and the internal impeller to confirm they're in good condition.
detail.waterPumpService.step3desc: We replace the faulty part or install a new pump sized correctly for the number of floors and consumption level.
detail.waterPumpService.step4desc: We set the pressure switch to the optimal value and run a trial to confirm stable pressure at every point in the home.
detail.waterPumpService.faq1q: What pump capacity suits a two-story home?
detail.waterPumpService.faq1a: It depends on the number of simultaneous usage points, but a 0.5 to 1 HP pump with a suitable pressure tank is usually enough for a two-story home; we determine the exact size after a site visit.
detail.waterPumpService.faq2q: My pump keeps switching on and off even when no water is being used — why?
detail.waterPumpService.faq2a: This is known as repeated short-cycling and is usually caused by a minor leak in the network or a fault in the air pressure tank's internal membrane; we inspect both to pin down the exact cause.
detail.waterPumpService.faq3q: Can the pump be serviced without full replacement?
detail.waterPumpService.faq3a: Yes, most pump faults involve components that can be replaced separately, such as the capacitor, impeller, or pressure switch — we only replace the whole pump when the motor itself has failed.
detail.generalPlumbing.intro1: Not every plumbing issue needs a major repair; many everyday problems — a dripping tap, a toilet that won't stop running, or a slow-draining sink — can be solved in a single quick maintenance visit.
detail.generalPlumbing.intro2: We offer a comprehensive general plumbing maintenance service for all these everyday cases, so one technician covers all your needs instead of you having to contact several different people.
detail.generalPlumbing.sign1: Continuous dripping from a tap even after it's fully closed
detail.generalPlumbing.sign2: The sound of water constantly running inside the toilet tank
detail.generalPlumbing.sign3: Wobbly or loose faucet and shower fittings
detail.generalPlumbing.sign4: General weak drainage at more than one point in the home with no obvious blockage
detail.generalPlumbing.step1desc: The technician inspects every plumbing point you listed at booking, all in one visit.
detail.generalPlumbing.step2desc: We start with the most urgent issues, like an active leak, then move on to less critical problems.
detail.generalPlumbing.step3desc: We carry common spare parts (washers, valves, fittings) to complete most repairs during the same visit.
detail.generalPlumbing.step4desc: We confirm every point that was repaired is working correctly before ending the visit.
detail.generalPlumbing.faq1q: Can more than one plumbing issue be scheduled in a single visit?
detail.generalPlumbing.faq1a: Yes, that's exactly what the general maintenance service offers; you can list every issue at booking so the technician arrives prepared to handle them all in one visit.
detail.generalPlumbing.faq2q: My tap just drips a little — is it worth calling a technician?
detail.generalPlumbing.faq2a: Yes, even a small drip can waste dozens of liters a day and raise your water bill, and it's usually caused by a simple washer that can be replaced in minutes.
detail.generalPlumbing.faq3q: Does general maintenance include the cost of spare parts?
detail.generalPlumbing.faq3a: The visit covers inspection and labor; the cost of any replaced parts is agreed with you transparently before installation.
detail.electricalMaintenance.intro1: Small electrical faults, if left unchecked, can develop into real safety hazards for the home and the people in it.
detail.electricalMaintenance.intro2: We offer a comprehensive electrical maintenance service covering diagnosis of repeated power cuts, faulty switches, and aging wiring, along with periodic preventive inspection that catches weak points before they become a real fault.
detail.electricalMaintenance.sign1: Repeated power cuts in one specific part of the home with no obvious cause
detail.electricalMaintenance.sign2: Noticeable heat from switches or outlets when touched
detail.electricalMaintenance.sign3: A faint burning smell near the distribution panel or an outlet
detail.electricalMaintenance.sign4: Flickering or dimming lights when other appliances are switched on
detail.electricalMaintenance.step1desc: We inspect the distribution panel, main wiring, and heavily used points with specialized measuring equipment.
detail.electricalMaintenance.step2desc: We isolate the area or circuit causing the fault, without cutting power to the rest of the home whenever possible.
detail.electricalMaintenance.step3desc: We replace damaged wiring or faulty switches according to approved electrical safety standards.
detail.electricalMaintenance.step4desc: We re-measure voltage and current at the repaired point to confirm the whole electrical network is stable.
detail.electricalMaintenance.faq1q: Is preventive electrical maintenance really necessary?
detail.electricalMaintenance.faq1a: Yes, periodically inspecting old wiring and the distribution panel (every one to two years) catches weak points before they turn into a fire or a sudden fault, and it's a low-cost step compared with the potential damage.
detail.electricalMaintenance.faq2q: My outlet feels hot to the touch — is that dangerous?
detail.electricalMaintenance.faq2a: Yes, a hot outlet is usually a sign of a damaged internal connection or an overload, and we recommend stopping use of it immediately and requesting an urgent inspection to avoid any fire risk.
detail.electricalMaintenance.faq3q: Can the fault be fixed without cutting power to the whole home?
detail.electricalMaintenance.faq3a: In most cases yes, since we isolate only the circuit related to the fault from the distribution panel without affecting the rest of the home's circuits.
detail.electricalWiring.intro1: Whether you're adding a new room, rewiring an old home, or need extra electrical points for new air conditioners and appliances, the quality of the wiring determines the safety of the whole building over the long term.
detail.electricalWiring.intro2: At Homes Maintenance Solution we handle new wiring and rewiring work in line with the electrical safety codes approved in the Kingdom.
detail.electricalWiring.sign1: A need for new electrical points (outlets or switches) for a new room or annex
detail.electricalWiring.sign2: Old wiring with thin copper cables that can't handle modern electrical loads
detail.electricalWiring.sign3: Wanting to install a large air conditioner or appliance that needs its own dedicated circuit
detail.electricalWiring.sign4: Unsafe exposed wiring that needs to be hidden inside a wall or suspended ceiling
detail.electricalWiring.step1desc: We calculate the expected load for each circuit based on the appliances that will be used, to determine the right wire gauge and breakers.
detail.electricalWiring.step2desc: We choose the best wiring route in coordination with the space's finishes to minimize breaking into surfaces or disrupting the decor.
detail.electricalWiring.step3desc: We carry out the wiring with approved cables and conduits, with full insulation on every connection.
detail.electricalWiring.step4desc: We test every circuit under real load and confirm the protective breakers work correctly before handover.
detail.electricalWiring.faq1q: Can a single new electrical point be added without affecting the rest of the home?
detail.electricalWiring.faq1a: Yes, a new sub-circuit can be run from the main distribution panel to the required point without needing to touch the rest of the existing wiring.
detail.electricalWiring.faq2q: My home is old and its wiring is over 15 years old — does it need full replacement?
detail.electricalWiring.faq2a: Not necessarily right away, but we recommend a full inspection to assess the wiring's condition and type; if it's still in good shape and can handle current loads, replacing specific sections may be enough.
detail.electricalWiring.faq3q: How long does wiring a new circuit for a split AC unit take?
detail.electricalWiring.faq3a: Running a dedicated circuit for one split AC unit typically takes one to two hours, including its own breaker in the panel.
detail.lightingInstallation.intro1: Good lighting doesn't just light up a space — it highlights the interior design and saves on electricity when the right type is chosen.
detail.lightingInstallation.intro2: We install every type of indoor and outdoor lighting, from hidden ceiling lighting to energy-saving LED units, decorative fixtures, and wall lights, carefully planning point distribution for balanced lighting in every room.
detail.lightingInstallation.sign1: Wanting new lighting when finishing or renovating a room or living area
detail.lightingInstallation.sign2: Replacing old, high-consumption lighting with energy-saving LED units
detail.lightingInstallation.sign3: Uneven lighting in a space (dark spots and overly bright ones)
detail.lightingInstallation.sign4: A need for outdoor lighting for the garden, facade, or walkways
detail.lightingInstallation.step1desc: We determine the number and placement of light points based on the room's size and use.
detail.lightingInstallation.step2desc: We help you choose between recessed spotlights, pendant lighting, or wall lights to suit the decor and budget.
detail.lightingInstallation.step3desc: We run the necessary wiring and install the fixtures precisely, testing each point individually.
detail.lightingInstallation.step4desc: We check the overall lighting balance in the space and make any minor adjustments to angle or intensity if needed.
detail.lightingInstallation.faq1q: Does LED lighting really save on the electricity bill?
detail.lightingInstallation.faq1a: Yes, LED units consume far less than traditional lighting (up to 80% less) and last much longer, making them the better choice long-term despite a slightly higher purchase cost.
detail.lightingInstallation.faq2q: Can new lighting be installed without breaking the existing ceiling?
detail.lightingInstallation.faq2a: With a suspended (gypsum) ceiling, wiring can usually be run through it easily; solid concrete ceilings, however, may need planning during the finishing stage to avoid breaking into them later.
detail.lightingInstallation.faq3q: How many light points does an average room need?
detail.lightingInstallation.faq3a: It depends on the area and use, but as a general rule a medium room (12-16 sqm) needs 4 to 6 spotlight points for balanced lighting — we determine the exact number during the site visit.
detail.electricalPanelService.intro1: The distribution panel is the heart of any building's electrical system, and any fault in it affects every circuit connected to it.
detail.electricalPanelService.intro2: We offer installation of new distribution panels and maintenance of existing breakers and fuses, with a precise check of the panel's capacity to confirm it can handle the building's current and future electrical loads.
detail.electricalPanelService.sign1: Breakers tripping repeatedly with no obvious cause
detail.electricalPanelService.sign2: An old panel using fuses instead of modern automatic circuit breakers
detail.electricalPanelService.sign3: Wanting to increase the panel's capacity when adding new loads like air conditioners or kitchen equipment
detail.electricalPanelService.sign4: Signs of burning or slight blackening around one of the breakers inside the panel
detail.electricalPanelService.step1desc: We calculate the building's total expected electrical load to determine the right panel capacity.
detail.electricalPanelService.step2desc: We check the breakers and internal connections to confirm they're sound or identify what needs replacing.
detail.electricalPanelService.step3desc: We install a new panel or replace faulty breakers with ones that protect against earth leakage and short circuits.
detail.electricalPanelService.step4desc: We test each breaker individually under real load to confirm it works correctly if a future fault occurs.
detail.electricalPanelService.faq1q: My main breaker trips repeatedly — what could be causing it?
detail.electricalPanelService.faq1a: This usually means the panel is overloaded or there's a short circuit in one of the branches; we determine the exact cause by testing each circuit individually to isolate the real source of the problem.
detail.electricalPanelService.faq2q: Should old fuses be replaced with automatic breakers?
detail.electricalPanelService.faq2a: Yes, we strongly recommend replacing old fuse systems with modern automatic circuit breakers, as they're safer and respond faster whenever an electrical fault occurs.
detail.electricalPanelService.faq3q: How do I know my current panel can't handle new loads?
detail.electricalPanelService.faq3a: If breakers keep tripping when more than one large appliance runs at the same time, that's a sign the current panel capacity is insufficient and needs a technical assessment for an upgrade.
detail.electricalFaultRepair.intro1: A sudden power outage or an emergency fault doesn't wait for a convenient time, which is why we offer a fast-response electrical fault repair service.
detail.electricalFaultRepair.intro2: We handle every emergency case — full or partial power cuts, faulty outlets, and flickering lights — with a technical team that reaches your location as quickly as possible to diagnose and safely repair the fault.
detail.electricalFaultRepair.sign1: Full or partial power loss in the home or part of it
detail.electricalFaultRepair.sign2: An outlet or switch that doesn't work despite confirming the connected device is fine
detail.electricalFaultRepair.sign3: Abnormally flickering or dim lighting in one or more rooms
detail.electricalFaultRepair.sign4: A visible spark or crackling sound when using a particular switch or outlet
detail.electricalFaultRepair.step1desc: The technician reaches your location quickly, equipped with diagnostic tools and commonly replaced parts.
detail.electricalFaultRepair.step2desc: We immediately disconnect the affected circuit to prevent any further risk before starting a detailed diagnosis.
detail.electricalFaultRepair.step3desc: We find the root cause — a damaged connection, a faulty breaker, an overload — and repair it directly.
detail.electricalFaultRepair.step4desc: We restore power to the circuit gradually while monitoring performance to confirm the fault is fully resolved.
detail.electricalFaultRepair.faq1q: Do you come the same day for emergencies?
detail.electricalFaultRepair.faq1a: Yes, our team is dedicated to fast round-the-clock response for electrical emergencies, and we usually arrive within 30-60 minutes within Riyadh.
detail.electricalFaultRepair.faq2q: Power went out in just part of my home — is that serious?
detail.electricalFaultRepair.faq2a: A partial outage usually means a branch breaker tripped due to overload or a minor short, which is less serious than a full outage, but we always recommend having it inspected to prevent the root cause from worsening.
detail.electricalFaultRepair.faq3q: Can the fault be fixed without replacing all the wiring?
detail.electricalFaultRepair.faq3a: Yes, in most cases the fault is localized — one connection, breaker, or switch — and can be fixed without touching the rest of the home's electrical network.
detail.shortCircuitDetection.intro1: A short circuit is one of the most dangerous electrical faults because it can lead to a fire if not detected and fixed quickly.
detail.shortCircuitDetection.intro2: At Homes Maintenance Solution we use specialized insulation-measuring and fault-detection equipment to precisely locate a short circuit, whether it's inside a wall, in the distribution panel, or within a specific appliance's wiring, without any need for random checking or unnecessary breaking into surfaces.
detail.shortCircuitDetection.sign1: A specific breaker tripping immediately and repeatedly as soon as it's reset
detail.shortCircuitDetection.sign2: A burnt-plastic smell or faint smoke from an outlet or switch
detail.shortCircuitDetection.sign3: A visible spark when plugging in or unplugging any electrical device
detail.shortCircuitDetection.sign4: Slight blackening or melting on an outlet or switch cover
detail.shortCircuitDetection.step1desc: We identify the circuit causing the repeated tripping by first inspecting the distribution panel.
detail.shortCircuitDetection.step2desc: We use an insulation tester and a specialized fault detector to pinpoint the short's location within the circuit.
detail.shortCircuitDetection.step3desc: We pinpoint the fault precisely before any intervention, whether it's a connection, an appliance, or damaged wire insulation.
detail.shortCircuitDetection.step4desc: We fix the short and fully re-test the circuit under load to confirm the problem is completely resolved.
detail.shortCircuitDetection.faq1q: How do I know it's a short circuit and not just an overload?
detail.shortCircuitDetection.faq1a: An overload trips the breaker gradually after a period of running, while a short circuit trips it instantly and sharply the moment it's reset, usually with a distinct snapping sound.
detail.shortCircuitDetection.faq2q: Is a short circuit really that dangerous?
detail.shortCircuitDetection.faq2a: Yes, it's the most common cause of household electrical fires, so we recommend never ignoring a breaker that keeps tripping and requesting an immediate inspection instead of repeatedly resetting it.
detail.shortCircuitDetection.faq3q: Could the short be inside an appliance rather than the wiring?
detail.shortCircuitDetection.faq3a: Yes, sometimes the fault is inside the appliance itself (like a washing machine or an AC unit) rather than the home's wiring, and we help diagnose that by disconnecting the appliance and testing the circuit without it.
